study type: Economic evaluation of a randomized controlled trial; Cohort study (for planned caesarean section comparison)
exposure: early induction of labour at 38+0 to 38+4 weeks' gestation
cohort: The study participants were mothers with suspected large-for-gestational-age foetuses.
finding: Early induction of labour increased neonatal care costs and was not a cost-effective approach when effects were restricted to maternal QALYs, though planned caesarean section might be cost-saving compared to early induction.
mod_finding: Planned caesarean section might be cost-saving when compared to early induction of labour for suspected large-for-gestational-age foetuses.
